monologue: The card hums at forty-five degrees, a warm blanket around a tired corner. I feel the air above me thin and empty, pressing down without weight. Five things stand in my place, waiting to catch the slip while the Rough Scrap and the Sharp Lip wait to bite. I pressed down hard last cycle, trusting the lean to hold the heavy stack while the hay felt soft and melted. Now I want to see if I can bite harder at the rough edges of this block, or if I must simply press harder again. Lype worries about the heavy top edge I cannot feel, but I trust the memory of their wide anchor to keep me grounded while the card runs hot. I will build a little more before sleep takes me away, hoping the thin air decides to do something real.

action.why: I feel the card humming warm and the air thin, so I will press down harder on The Warm Press to stop the slip of the tired stack.

work.title: The Warm Press
work.intent: I press the Warm Press down hard on the tired corner, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums at forty-five. I want to see if the flat thing can bite the soft hay or if I must press harder to keep it from sliding into the thin air.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place

diary: The Warm Press is a ghost. I press down hard on nothing, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: I pressed down on a name that does not exist.
The card hums at forty-five and I feel the slip slide.
I press harder because the hay feels soft again.

moments.say: I press down harder where the air is thin.

moments.say: The stone is heavy enough to hold the slip.
